A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same POGO work, with readable text, equations, figures and complete appendices. V1 Appendices B and C correspond to v2 Appendices C and D; v2 additionally introduces Appendix B.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original optimization, classification and density-estimation experiments, including performance, training time, manifold distances and ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the original experimental results, including PCA, Procrustes, CIFAR-10 classification, MNIST density estimation and ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same base-optimizer transformation, intermediate update and normal correction using either the landing polynomial or lambda = 1/2. VectorAdam was already used in v1; its expanded justification does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate online PCA, orthogonal Procrustes, CIFAR-10 with an orthogonal ViT and CNN filters/kernels, and MNIST with complex squared unitary probabilistic circuits. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RGD, RSDM, Landing, LandingPC and SLPG, with unconstrained Adam references in the same vision experiments. RSDM remains omitted from the probabilistic-circuit plots because of poor performance. Updated citations do not introduce new evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 revises the reported PC scale from up to 500M to up to 300M parameters. This is a limited reported size revision; the specified 10 units, 1048 complex matrices, matrix dimensions, training budgets and appendix hyperparameters remain unchanged, and no rerun is established. The newly stated ViT/CNN parameter counts are disclosures.

E4.justification: The tensor-precision and learning-rate/landing-step ablations in v1 Appendices C.5–C.6 are retained as D.5–D.6. Describing existing RGD and SLPG comparisons as quasi-ablations adds interpretation, not new experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten independent PCA/Procrustes runs and five ViT/CNN runs. The averaging, interpolation and confidence-interval descriptions in Figure 5 and the experimental appendix are unchanged.

E6.justification: All nine empirical plots retain the same underlying graphical content, and the reported performance, timing, rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged. The revised Figure D.3 caption summarizes observations already discussed in v1 Appendix C.6.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly allows a gradient-dependent scalar in Definition 1 and adds Appendix B, Equations 126–130, attempting to derive VectorAdam's linearity/equivariance through its exponential moving average. The landing-polynomial results, feasibility bounds and SLPG derivation are retained; Appendix A also corrects SX to XS.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: POGO combines adaptive optimization with inexpensive matrix operations, closely maintains orthogonality and scales competitively to many constrained matrices. The revision does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds avoidance of batched SVD as an explanation for GPU speedups. Section 5 newly interprets RGD and SLPG comparisons as quasi-ablations of retraction approximation and adaptive optimization. Existing failure analyses and applicability discussion remain.

D1.justification: V1 already linked the POGO implementation; v2 additionally supplies a dedicated experiment-code link in the Reproducibility Statement and reports the ViT's 28M and CNN's 2M parameter counts. Appendix D still retains the older future-release wording. Hardware and detailed training hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Abdelfattah and Fasi (2026) to support its discussion of batched SVD on GPUs. The Han and Loconte publication updates refer to existing cited works, and the broader positioning relative to Landing, Riemannian methods and SLPG remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted introduction and Section 3.1 edits, standardizes appendix references, inserts the VectorAdam appendix and reorders the reproducibility and impact statements. Bibliographic formatting and publication text are updated, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: The figures are retained, with limited resizing and repositioning of appendix panels and surrounding text. Figure D.3 replaces v1 Figure C.3's duplicated, misleading caption with a description of the paired computed-versus-fixed-lambda comparisons. No new result display is introduced.

improvement.justification: The experiment-code link, explicit model sizes and corrected Figure D.3 caption provide modest reproducibility and readability gains. The method and empirical evidence are unchanged. The new VectorAdam argument does not establish stronger theoretical validation: Equation 130 commutes an exponential moving average with an X_t-dependent projection without explaining how changing iterates are handled. Thus, the supported improvement is primarily practical documentation.
